comments.author: @OrionHidden
comments.text: Many people are surprised to learn that Timbuktu was once one of the world's greatest centers of learning, with thousands of handwritten manuscripts preserving knowledge in astronomy, medicine, mathematics, law, and philosophy. Africa's history is far richer than many realize.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: Thank you - that reputation as a center of scholarship, not just trade, is exactly the perception gap we wanted to close.

comments.author: @PlanetUncoveredOfficial
comments.text: It’s fascinating that the Dogon people are said to have known about Sirius B long before Western astronomers discovered it. I’d love to know how that knowledge was passed down through generations.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: It's a fascinating claim, though worth knowing it's genuinely contested among anthropologists - some researchers argue the "Sirius mystery" may trace back to information passed to the Dogon by 20th-century European visitors rather than ancient independent knowledge. Either way, Dogon cosmology itself is remarkably rich on its own terms.
